key_insight: QSTAR shows that quantum heads are most useful as selective fallback branches for uncertain inputs, not as direct replacements for strong classical classifiers.
engineering_relevance: For hybrid quantum–classical systems, adaptive routing can improve overall transfer-learning performance while limiting quantum computation to samples where it adds value.
method: Freeze a ResNet18 backbone on Fashion-MNIST.
Compare manual QTL heads, KetGPT-designed quantum heads, and parameter-matched classical baselines under the same split and training setup.
Route high-confidence predictions through the classical path and send low-confidence samples to a fallback quantum branch.
evidence_signal: On the filtered sweep, the strongest KetGPT head reached 78.5% accuracy and 0.785 F1, while Adaptive KetGPT-QTL achieved 80.9% accuracy and 0.807 F1 on the full system.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on a single dataset with a frozen backbone, so the gains may not generalize to broader tasks, larger models, or more noisy quantum hardware settings.
paper_title: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing
